rubrics.justification: The response accurately describes the 3BB blastocyst features including expanded blastocoel with thinned zona, loosely compacted ICM, and sparse TE layer. The description aligns well with the Gardner grading provided. Minor limitation is acknowledging image uncertainty rather than providing fully confident morphological assessment, but this is appropriate epistemic humility rather than an error.

Excellent integration of all major clinical factors. The response systematically connects age (31) to chromosomal competence, BMI 40.4 to implantation and obstetric risk, endometriosis to oocyte quality and endometrial environment, smoking to implantation and miscarriage risk, prior failed cycles to prognosis adjustment, and semen parameters to male factor assessment. Interactions between factors (e.g., obesity+endometriosis+smoking compounding risk despite young age) are clearly articulated.

The reasoning is highly coherent and internally consistent. The probability estimate of 25-40% implantation logically follows from balancing the favorable factors (age 31, good reserve, adequate endometrium) against the adverse factors (BMI, smoking, endometriosis, prior failures, moderate embryo grade). The lower live birth estimate (18-30%) appropriately accounts for additional loss risk. No contradictions identified throughout the lengthy response.

Response aligns well with ESHRE/ASRM guidelines: recommends single embryo transfer at age 31 per elective SET guidelines, appropriately cautions against routine surgical intervention for endometriosis given ovarian reserve risk, correctly positions PGT-A as non-mandatory at age 31, recommends hysteroscopy/cavity assessment after repeated failures, and appropriately discusses freeze-all strategy for endometriosis patients. Smoking cessation and weight loss recommendations align with evidence-based preconception guidance.

Highly actionable with specific recommendations for both current transfer (SET, luteal support optimization, smoking cessation, metabolic workup including HbA1c and thyroid) and future planning (hysteroscopy, adenomyosis assessment, chronic endometritis evaluation, FET consideration, sperm DNA fragmentation if blastulation poor, PGT-A discussion if failures continue). Recommendations are appropriately nuanced with clear rationale and alternatives considered for each decision point.
